messages.author: 9bb998c1d862319e
messages.subject: problem starting (restarting) shiny-server after update
parts:
Dear crew,

First, I did do a search on this topic.  I found one possibly-related entry but it was a different OS and slightly different situation and the answer did not seem to resolve my situation.

Issue --

I recently upgraded from shiny-server v1.2.0 to v1.3.0.  I believe that I followed the instructions in the administrator's guide under migrating and updating.

My shiny-server is running on a corporate Linux server that uses Red Hat Enterprise release 6.5.

I updated using rpm and shiny-server-1.3.0.403-rh5-x86_64.rpm
Prior to this, I also reinstalled the latest version of R (3.1.2) and the shiny package (0.11).  The system worked after updating R and shiny.

Prior to the update of shiny-server things were running pretty well.  Love the package.  And for a couple of days after the update things also seemed to be working reasonably well.  I started to have an issue after a stop/start of the server (using sudo stop, sudo start, and also tried sudo restart).  When I try to restart the shiny-server, I get the message:

"start: Unknown job: shiny-server"

I checked for the shiny-server.conf file in the /etc/shiny-server/ directory and it is there.

Is the issue maybe related to the change in the default hosting directory?  Or something else?

Thank you in advance for any guidance.

Cliff

messages.author: 3da48b33a2f506a9
messages.subject: Re: problem starting (restarting) shiny-server after update
parts:
Hi Cliff,

What command have you used to start? To be sure, you should be using:

sudo start shiny-server

If this doesn't work, can you check for the following file:

/etc/init/shiny-server.conf

And can you also give the output of this command:

sed -nr "s/.*release\\ ([0-9]).*/\\1/p" /etc/redhat-release

Thanks,
Fereshteh

messages.author: 3da48b33a2f506a9
messages.subject: Re: problem starting (restarting) shiny-server after update
parts:
Cliff,

If running on Red Hat Enterprise release 6.5 (as you are), there should be 2 config files, with same names:
/etc/shiny-server/shiny-server.conf
/etc/init/shiny-server.conf

You have the first one, which is for configuring runtime of Shiny Server.
The second one (missing from your system) is an Upstart file, for controlling stop/start of Shiny Server as a service. 
I just tried the same binary on Red Hat Enterprise release 6.5, and it works fine. May be something went wrong during your installation. Do you mind uninstalling Shiny Server, and installing again using the same rpm. See if you get any errors during installation.

And please check for /etc/init/shiny-server.conf file after install is completed.

Fereshteh
